incidentsResolved: Headless MV3 verification initially used Playwright's reduced headless shell. Ferrum now uses the full chromium channel for extension-capable headless runs.
Lightpanda through Playwright timed out on Chromium lifecycle expectations. Ferrum now drives Lightpanda through its native CDP server directly.
Parallel runs could collide on evidence directory IDs. Evidence IDs now include a random nonce.
Benchmark warmup 0 was coerced to 1. Explicit zero warmup is now preserved.

Cross-platform checkout line endings produced different fixture hashes. Repository text checkout is normalized to LF and Linux/Windows extension SHA-256 matched exactly at the prior byte-verified checkpoint.
Workbench ephemeral port mode originally reported port 0 instead of the bound port. The server now reports the actual assigned port.

A Chromium favicon request exposed missing static assets being returned as HTTP 500. Ferrum now returns a truthful 404 for missing assets and the Workbench uses an inline data favicon; the behavior is regression-tested.
Extension worker observability previously stopped at discovery and messaging. Ferrum now records worker console/network/failure/interception evidence and asserts it across restart.

Successful CLI and MCP runs could flood agent context while making the evidence directory harder to discover. Ferrum now emits compact actionable summaries by default where requested, always preserves full disk evidence, and exposes the exact evidence directory.
Electron existed as an implementation-only target. It is now runtime-qualified against a real secure preload/renderer/main IPC application on Ubuntu and Windows.

Benchmark timing lacked enough context for trustworthy cross-host comparisons. Ferrum now records machine/runtime context, workload and step budgets, success rate, timeout count, and per-sample evidence directories.
